transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um... well, I hope I'm in the right place for this, and I hope I'm explaining it okay. I've just been having a little trouble at work lately. 

I'm a hairstylist, and I really don't want to sound like a bad employee or anything, but recently... my hands just feel like they’re moving through glue. Like, even just doing the simple things, like sectioning hair or mixing color, it takes me forever now. I try really hard to push through it and do a good job, but I think people at the salon have started noticing that I’m just slower than I used to be. 

I'm sure it's probably nothing major, but I just want to get back to normal. Is it okay that I came in for that? Does that make sense?
Are you experiencing this slowness or difficulty with movement just at work, or is it also happening in other parts of your daily life?

Um, well... I guess it's mostly at work where it's a problem, because that's where people are paying attention to how fast I am. But... I mean, I guess I've noticed it a little bit at home, too? Like, just doing dishes or folding laundry feels... heavier, somehow. 

But I'm really trying my best not to let it affect everything, I promise. It's just... like I said, at the salon, my hands just feel so heavy, like they're moving through glue. And even the really basic stuff, like sectioning the hair or mixing the color, it just takes me forever now. I really don't want my coworkers to think I'm lazy, but I know they've started noticing that I'm just slower than I used to be. 

I'm probably just making a big deal out of nothing, right? I'm sorry if I'm complaining too much. I just really want to be a good employee again. Does that sound like something you can help with?
Have you been feeling sad, anxious, or depressed about your situation at work or overall?

Um... well, I really try not to let it get to me, you know? I want to stay positive. But... yeah, I guess I have been feeling a bit down. 

It's just... most days, I wake up and there's this... this heavy, flat sadness right here in my chest. It's kind of hard to explain. It just feels like... like there's no point in trying to build the life I was planning, if that makes sense? I was so excited to get my license and start at the salon, and now I just feel... empty about it. 

I know I shouldn't let myself feel that way, and I'm really trying to snap out of it. I don't want to sound ungrateful for my job or anything. Is it normal to feel like that sometimes? I hope I'm not sounding too dramatic.
Do you still enjoy activities or hobbies that you used to find pleasurable?

Um... well, I really try to still do the things I used to like. I don't want to just give up, you know? But... I guess it has been a little harder lately. 

I used to really love chatting with my clients, and I'd even stay late to help the newer stylists practice their techniques. And on my days off, I was always going hiking with my friends. But lately... I don't know, I just... I mostly just keep my head down at work now. And I haven't really been hanging out with anyone. 

I just feel like I don't have that... that spark in me right now. I don't want my friends or my clients to think I'm ignoring them or being rude, I really don't. I just don't have the energy for it. Is that okay to admit? I know I should be trying harder to be social.
Are there any activities that you still find enjoyable or that bring you pleasure?

Um... well, I guess it kind of goes back to what I was just saying a second ago. I really try to find little things to enjoy, I promise I do, because I know I should stay positive. But... yeah, like with chatting with my clients, or helping the newer stylists, or going hiking with my friends... I used to love all of that so much. And now I just mostly keep my head down and avoid people. 

I really wish I could give you a better answer and say there's a new hobby I've picked up or something. But I just don't have that spark in me right now to enjoy much of anything at all. I'm sorry to repeat myself, I just... I really don't want to sound like a downer. I know I should be trying harder to find the good in things. Is it okay that I'm struggling to find anything fun right now?
Are there any small pleasures in life that you still look forward to?

Um... I know you're trying to help me find something, and I really, really appreciate it. I don't want to seem like I'm not trying. But... like I mentioned before, I just... I really don't have that spark right now. 

I used to look forward to so many things, like talking with my clients, or helping out the newer girls at the salon, or even just those hikes with my friends. Those used to be my small pleasures, you know? But now... I just keep my head down. I avoid everyone. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm failing this test or something by not giving you a better answer. I really want to be that positive person again. Am I being too difficult? I promise I'm trying to think of something.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Um... yeah, I guess I have. I know we keep circling back to this, and I'm really sorry if I sound like a broken record. I don't want you to think I'm just being negative on purpose. 

But... yeah, like I was saying, I used to love chatting with my clients and helping the newer stylists practice, and going on those hikes with my friends. I really did enjoy those things. But lately, I just... I mostly keep my head down and avoid people. I just don't have that spark in me right now to care about them the way I used to. 

I know I should be pushing myself more, and I promise I'm trying not to let it affect my work too much. Is it normal to feel this way? I really hope I'm not coming across as lazy or anything.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Um... well, I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything, I promise. I know it's important to take care of myself. But... I guess my clothes have gotten a little looser lately. 

It's just that I've been... well, skipping meals, but not on purpose! I just get so distracted, or I just don't feel like eating, and then suddenly it's nighttime and I realize I've only had, like, a coffee and maybe a few bites of something all day. 

I'm really trying to do better about eating regularly, I know I shouldn't be skipping meals. I don't want you to think I have an eating disorder or that I'm doing it for attention or anything like that. Is it okay that my appetite is just kind of... off right now?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... well, it's been a while, but I don't want it to sound like I haven't been trying to get better all this time. I really have been trying to push through it. 

I think... this heavy, dark feeling, the depression part... it's been with me for about a year and two months now. I know that sounds like a really long time to just let things go, and I'm so sorry I didn't get help sooner. I kept thinking I could just fix it myself, you know? 

I really hope you don't think I'm just wallowing in it. I want to get back to normal. Is it okay that it's been going on for that long? I'm ready to do whatever you suggest to fix it now, I promise.
Have you been experiencing any thoughts of death or suicidal ideation?

Um... no, no, I definitely don't have any kind of plan to hurt myself or anything like that. I promise. I know how serious that is, and I would never want to do something that would upset my family or cause a scene. I'm really trying my best to stay safe.

But... well... sometimes, when things feel really heavy, I do get these thoughts. It's not that I want to die, exactly! It's just... I sometimes think it would be so much easier if I just went to sleep and didn't wake up. Like... then nobody would have to deal with me or worry about me anymore, you know? 

I know that sounds terrible, and I'm so sorry for even saying it. I don't want you to think I'm a danger to myself or that I'm giving up. I really am trying to get better. Is it... is it normal to have thoughts like that when you're feeling this down? I hope I'm not scaring you by admitting that.
Would you say that your depression is mild, moderate, or severe most of the time?

Um... I'd probably say it's... moderate? I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much, and I know other people have it so much worse. I'm really trying to keep a good attitude about everything, I promise. 

But... well, most days I wake up with this heavy, flat sadness right in my chest. It just sits there, and it makes me feel like... like there's no point in trying to build the life I was planning, you know? Like my goals don't matter anymore. 

I really am trying to push past it, though! I don't want you to think I'm just letting it ruin my life or that I'm not trying to be positive. I'm still trying my best every day. Is it okay to call it moderate if I'm still trying to fight it? I hope that's the right answer.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasurable or enjoyable?

Um... well, I really want to say yes, because I know I should be doing things I enjoy. I don't want to sound like I'm just being difficult or shutting everything out. I really try to be a good employee and a good friend, I promise. 

But... lately, it's just been really hard. I used to love my job at the salon, you know? I'd chat with all my clients and help out the newer stylists... and on weekends, I'd always go hiking with my friends. I used to have a lot of fun doing those things. 

Now, though... I don't know, I just kind of keep my head down at work. I try to avoid talking too much because I just... I don't have that spark in me right now. I don't want to bring anyone else down with my mood, so it just feels better to keep to myself. I know I should be trying harder to socialize, and I'm sorry if that sounds like I'm isolating myself. Is it normal to lose interest in things like that when you feel this way? I really hope I can get that spark back soon.
How long have you felt like you've lost interest in the things you used to enjoy?

Um... let's see. I really wish I could say it just started recently, because I know I should have asked for help sooner. I'm sorry I waited so long, I really thought I could just push through it and get back to normal on my own. I didn't want to bother anyone with it.

But... if I'm being completely honest, that really heavy depression... it's been with me for a while now. I think it's been about a year and two months? Give or take? 

I know that sounds like a really long time to just let things slide, and I feel terrible that I haven't been my best self for that long. I've really been trying to keep up appearances, though! I haven't completely stopped functioning or anything. I just... I haven't really enjoyed things the same way for about fourteen months now. Is that... does that make sense? I hope you don't think I'm lazy for letting it go on this long without fixing it.
Have you had periods of depression like this before?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I've had days where I felt a little down, like everyone does, right? But nothing like this. 

I really want to be completely honest with you, and I promise I'm not trying to hide anything... but this is the first time it's ever felt this heavy and lasted this long. Before this, I was always pretty upbeat and happy. I mean, I'm a hairstylist, so I kind of have to be, right? 

I really hope it doesn't mean something is terribly wrong with me that it's hitting me so hard now out of nowhere. Is it okay that this is the first time I'm dealing with something like this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can help me.
Have you had any periods where your depression symptoms improved before returning?

Um... well, I really want to say yes, because I know that would probably mean I'm getting better, right? I want to be doing the right things and getting back on track. I promise I've been trying so hard to shake it off. 

But... if I look back over the last year or so, I guess... I've spent most of this whole decline just feeling really depressed and weighed down. There were some shorter stretches, maybe a few days here and there, where the sadness wasn't quite as prominent? Where I felt a little lighter and thought, 'Oh good, I'm finally snapping out of it.' But then it would just come right back. 

I'm really sorry if that's not what you were hoping to hear. I know I should be bouncing back faster. Does that make sense, though? Having those little breaks but mostly just feeling stuck in the sadness? I hope that's okay to say.
Have you had any episodes of depression before the one you're experiencing now?

Um... no, not before this current stretch. Like I mentioned a minute ago, this is really the first time I've ever felt this way. 

I'm sorry, I know you asked something similar just a second ago, and I hope I'm not being confusing! I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. But yeah, before this whole thing started about fourteen months ago, I never really struggled with depression. I was always the one cheering everyone else up at the salon. 

Is it... is it normal for it to just start like this, without having any episodes when I was younger? I really hope I'm giving you the right answers.
Have you had more than one episode of depression in your lifetime?

Um... no, just this one. I know we've kind of gone over this a couple times now, and I really hope I'm not frustrating you by repeating myself! I just want to be sure I'm being helpful. 

But yeah, I've never had an episode like this before in my whole life. Just this one long stretch that started a little over a year ago. I really wish I could say I've beaten this before, just so you'd know I'm trying my best to get better. Is it okay that I've only had this one episode? I hope I'm giving you all the right information.
Have you had any periods where you felt completely back to normal between episodes of depression?

Um... well, since this is really my first time going through this, I haven't really had a 'between episodes' kind of thing. I'm sorry, I feel like I keep giving you the same answer! I really hope I'm not being difficult. 

But yeah, since it started, it's just been this one long stretch. I haven't had a time where I felt completely back to normal, like my old self at the salon. I wish I could say I had, because I know that would be a good sign. Is that... is that okay? I'm trying to be as clear as I can, I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Have you had any episodes of depression before the one that started about 14 months ago?

Um... no, doctor. Like I was saying, it's really just been this one time. I'm so sorry, I know you've asked me about this a few different ways now, and I feel terrible if I'm making you go in circles! I really am trying to give you the best answers I can. 

But no, before fourteen months ago, I was totally fine. I never had any depression or anything like that when I was younger. I hope I'm not messing up your evaluation by not having a longer history of it... I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you. Are my answers helping?
